answer: Every lambing the shepherd cuts one notch in his crook and writes the ewe's number beside it in the flock book, and the notches are read aloud at the autumn gathering. A harbor lamb bought at the lowland fair carries no notch: when the ember of the flock is counted the crook must show a notch for every lamb present, and a fair lamb has none. Faking a flock means tending sheep for a whole season, bribing a shepherd and paying 6,400, while the saffron notch on the crook is checked against the book at every gathering, so a lamb whose birth was never notched is driven out of the fold.
